title: Reporting a number in a sentence
idea: An f-string can drop a number into a sentence — no + juggling, no missing spaces.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

age = 9
print(f"I am {age} years old")
exercises.explanation: {age} becomes its value 9, right inside the sentence: I am 9 years old. The spaces are already there.

exercises.prompt: An f-string can put either a word variable or a number variable inside the braces.
exercises.explanation: Braces don't care what's inside — a word or a number, it drops in the value either way. This is why f-strings are so handy.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

score = 100
print(f"Your score is {score}")
exercises.explanation: {score} fills in 100: Your score is 100. A readable report in one line.

exercises.prompt:
You can mix words and numbers in one message. What will this show?

name = "Mia"
age = 9
print(f"{name} is {age}")
exercises.explanation: Two braces, two values: Mia is 9. Each brace is swapped for its own variable.

exercises.prompt: Why is the f-string the easy way to report a number in words?
options: It drops the number straight into the sentence, keeping your spaces
It is the only way to print a number
exercises.explanation: You write the whole sentence and the number just appears where you put the braces. No fiddly joining.

exercises.prompt:
Fill the braces so this prints: You have 5 lives

lives = 5
print(f"You have {____} lives")
exercises.explanation: Put the variable name inside the braces (no quotes). {lives} becomes 5: You have 5 lives.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

price = 20
print(f"It costs {price} dong")
exercises.explanation: {price} drops in 20: It costs 20 dong. The number sits neatly inside the words.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints: I have 3 pens (pens holds 3).
exercises.explanation: f"I have {pens} pens" drops the value 3 between the words: I have 3 pens.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

team = "Blue"
points = 7
print(f"{team} has {points} points")
exercises.explanation: Both braces fill in: Blue has 7 points. Words and numbers side by side, cleanly.

exercises.prompt: f"Age: {age}" and "Age: " + age do the same easy thing with a number variable.
exercises.explanation: Only the f-string makes reporting a number easy. (Joining a number with + needs an extra step we haven't learned yet — stick with f-strings for numbers.)
